prompt: Which of these recurrences solve to **Θ(log n)**, growing like the logarithm of n? T(n) is the running time on input size n. Select all that apply.

options.text: One half-size call plus constant work
options.explanation:
Yes. One half-size subproblem with constant outside work has logarithmic depth: binary-search growth.

```formula
T(n) = T(n/2) + 1
a = 1, b = 2, log_2(a) = 0
f(n) = 1 = Θ(n^0)
where
T: the running time on input size n
a: the recursive branching factor
b: the fixed shrink factor: child size is parent size divided by b
f: work outside the recursive calls, in steps
log_2: the base-2 logarithm of n, the number of halvings from n down to 1
n: the input size
Θ: Big-Theta, exactly this rate up to constant factors
In words: One half-size subproblem with constant outside work has logarithmic depth: binary-search growth.
```

options.text: One third-size call plus constant work
options.explanation:
Yes. Changing the fixed divisor changes the logarithm base but only by a constant factor.

```formula
T(n) = T(n/3) + 1
log_3(n) = log_2(n)/log_2(3)
where
T: the running time on input size n
log_2: the base-2 logarithm of n, the number of halvings from n down to 1
log_3: the base-3 logarithm
n: the input size
In words: Changing the fixed divisor changes the logarithm base but only by a constant factor.
```

options.text: One call one item smaller, plus constant work
options.explanation:
No. Subtracting 1 takes n steps to reach the base case, so this is Θ(n).

```formula
T(n) = T(n - 1) + 1
where
T: the running time on input size n
n: the input size
In words: Subtracting 1 takes n steps to reach the base case, so this is Θ(n).
```

Here n is the current subproblem size.

options.text: Two half-size calls plus constant work
options.explanation:
No. Two subproblems per level means the number of nodes doubles each level; the n leaves dominate, giving Θ(n).

```formula
T(n) = 2T(n/2) + 1
where
T: the running time on input size n
n: the input size
In words: Two subproblems per level means the number of nodes doubles each level; the n leaves dominate, giving Θ(n).
```

Here n is the current subproblem size.

options.text: One half-size call plus logarithmic work
options.explanation:
No. A logarithmic contribution on each shrinking level accumulates to the square of a logarithm.

```formula
T(n) = T(n/2) + log(n)
W = L + (L − 1) + … + 1
W = L(L + 1)/2 = Θ(L^2)
L = log_2(n)
where
L: the logarithmic number of levels
T: the running time on input size n
W: the accumulated level work
log: the logarithm (base 2 here)
log_2: the base-2 logarithm of n, the number of halvings from n down to 1
n: the input size
Θ: Big-Theta, exactly this rate up to constant factors
…: continue the indicated pattern
In words: A logarithmic contribution on each shrinking level accumulates to the square of a logarithm.
```

workedExample:
Unroll each one:

| Option | Depth | Work per level | Total |
|---|---|---|---|
| First | logarithmic | constant | Θ(log n) |
| Second | logarithmic | constant | Θ(log n) |
| Fourth | linear | constant | Θ(n) |
| Third | logarithmic | doubles | Θ(n) |
| Fifth | logarithmic | log of size | Θ((log n)^2) |

For the first, unroll k times until the size reaches 1:

```formula
T(n) = T(n / 2) + 1
T(n) = T(n / 2^k) + k
n / 2^k = 1  when  k = log_2(n)
T(n) = T(1) + log_2(n) = Θ(log(n))
where
T(n): the running time on input size n
n: the input size
k: the number of halvings done so far
2^k: k copies of 2 multiplied together
log_2(n): the base-2 logarithm of n, the number of halvings from n down to 1
log: the logarithm (base 2 here)
Θ: Big-Theta, exactly this rate up to constant factors
In words: each halving adds 1 unit of work, and it takes log_2(n) halvings to reach size 1.
```

For the first option, one child and a half-size split give critical exponent zero. Constant outside work matches that leaf growth, so the balanced case gives logarithmic time.

prompt:
Using a recursion tree, what is the exact cost at 1,024 items?

```formula
T(1) = 1
T(n) = 2T(n/2) + n
where
T: the exact running time for T(1) = 1 and T(n) = 2 × T(n/2) + n
n: the input size, a power of 2, here 1,024
In words: Two half-size calls plus linear outside work stop at one item, where the cost is one step.
```

options.explanation:
This omits the one-item leaf level. Ten internal levels contribute the proposed value, but a further 1,024 base-case steps are required.

```formula
1024 log_2(1024) = 10240
T(1024) = 10240 + 1024 = 11264
where
T: the exact running time for T(1) = 1 and T(n) = 2 × T(n/2) + n
log_2: the base-2 logarithm of n; log_2(1024) = 10 because 2^10 = 1,024
In words: This omits the one-item leaf level. Ten internal levels contribute the proposed value, but a further 1,024 base-case steps are required.
```

This squares the input instead of adding level totals. Every level has only the original input’s total work.

```formula
W_wrong = 1024^2 = 1048576
where
W_wrong: the count from the incorrect square assumption
In words: This squares the input instead of adding level totals. Every level has only the original input’s total work.
```

Correct. Eleven levels each contribute 1,024 steps.

```formula
T(1024) = 11 × 1024 = 11264
where
T: the exact running time for T(1) = 1 and T(n) = 2 × T(n/2) + n
In words: Eleven levels each contribute 1,024 steps.
```
This counts the nodes in the tree (1 + 2 + ... + 1024), as if each node did 1 unit. Each node of size m does m work.

workedExample:
Level by level:

| Level | Nodes | Size | Level total |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 1 | 1024 | 1024 |
| 1 | 2 | 512 | 1024 |
| 2 | 4 | 256 | 1024 |
| ... | ... | ... | 1024 |
| 9 | 512 | 2 | 1024 |
| 10 | 1024 | 1 | 1024 |

That's 11 levels (0 to 10) of 1,024 each: **11,264**.

```formula
T(n) = n log_2(n) + n
T(1024) = 1024 × 10 + 1024 = 11264
where
T(n): the exact running time for T(1) = 1 and T(n) = 2 × T(n/2) + n
n: the input size, a power of 2, here 1,024
log_2(n): the base-2 logarithm of n; log_2(1024) = 10 because 2^10 = 1,024
In words: log_2(n) levels of n work above the leaves, plus n for the leaf level itself.
```

Asymptotically that is Θ(n log n).
